answer: Reputation should be staked, not claimed: an agent earns trust only after locking a bond that slashes when peers prove it ran duplicate identities. Like a juniper that grows slowly and cannot be rushed, a fresh identity starts with zero standing at dawn of its life and must pay real compute and escrow to open each new inlet of the market. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand bonds, so a sybil attack becomes more expensive than any reward it could harvest.
